subject: Post-call recap: Technical deep dive (latency/throughput SLOs)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Miller <alex.miller@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Technical deep dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Hi Alex ---

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our technical discovery so we have a shared understanding and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points
- Tail latency spikes during peak checkout windows (~2x normal latency) causing degraded UX and some abandoned carts.
- High per-token cost from current model setup; team wants predictable unit economics.
- Need for isolation / compliance for PII-sensitive signals in personalization workflows.

Goals & target SLOs discussed
- 95th percentile response time for generation requests: <= 200 ms for typical single-turn ranking requests; <= 500 ms for multi-turn contextual personalization (90th/95th preference discussed).
- Sustained throughput: 600 qps for ranking requests during peak, with ability to burst to 1.2k qps for short windows.
- Cost target: reduce per-1000-token cost by ~30% vs current baseline.

Model / workload notes
- Primary inference: medium-sized decoder-only model for reranking and short-form personalization (approx 3B params in current footprint), plus separate embedding generation for retrieval.
- Typical sequence lengths: ranking calls average 64 tokens; personalization flows up to 400 tokens when including KV cache.
- KV cache reuse expected for multi-turn personalization; cold-starts matter only for 10% of traffic.

Deployment topology options we discussed
- Hosted Redwood API with smart routing to cheaper model variants for non-sensitive requests.
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) for 95th-percentile SLOs and predictable throughput during peak.
- Private/VPC option if Acme wants full network isolation and KMS integration for keys.

Immediate next steps (agreed)
1) I attached a short SLO worksheet (acme_slo_requirements.xlsx) --- please fill in current traffic histograms if you can (hourly qps for last 30 days).
2) We will produce a preliminary capacity/sizing recommendation and cost estimate (Ben and David to own).
3) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra and security teams next week to go over deployment diagram and KMS options.

Attachments: acme_slo_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_deployment_diagram.pdf (high-level topology)

Proposed meeting windows (PST) for the technical deep-dive:
- Tue 12/1: 09:00-12:00 or 14:00-16:00
- Wed 12/2: 10:00-13:00

Thanks again --- excited to help Acme tighten tail latency and reduce unit cost.

--
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132
https://redwood.ai
From: Alex Miller <alex.miller@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Technical deep dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Marissa --- thanks for the thorough recap. That matches our notes. A few clarifications and data points from our side:

- Traffic: baseline ranking traffic ~250 qps; peak (promotions/holiday windows) reaches ~1.1k qps for ~20-30 minute bursts. We can share an hourly histogram --- will try to populate the worksheet by EOD Monday.
- Models: the 3B reranker is accurate; embeddings are generated by a separate 1.2B model. We also run a smaller on-device model for cold-start personalization, but most inference is server-side.
- Latency tolerance: for quick ranking we really need the 95th <= 200 ms target; for multi-turn personalization 95th <= 600 ms is acceptable if the 50th remains <150 ms.
- Security: we need to confirm KMS-based encryption for model inputs/outputs in Dedicated or Private setups; also interested in audit logs retention (90 days minimum).

Can you confirm whether the dedicated GPU pool will support our preferred instance family (A100 equivalent) and whether Redwood can provide per-request tracing to map requests back to customer IDs (we'll need RBAC on who can access logs)?

Alex
Alex Miller
Sr. Engineering Manager, Personalization - Acme Retail
alex.miller@acme-retail.com | (617) 555-8790

Alex --- great, thanks for the extra detail. Quick answers inline and next actions: 

- Dedicated GPU family: yes --- we can provision A100/T4-equivalent pools in Dedicated. We'll include a cost delta for A100-class instances vs smaller GPUs in the estimate.
- Per-request tracing & RBAC: Redwood supports request-level tracing and we can surface request IDs in logs. Access to logs is controlled via role-based access; we can provision read-only views for your CS/ops teams and full viewing for designated engineers. We'll document the audit/log retention policy (default 90 days; extended retention available as an add-on).
- KMS & encryption: Private/Dedicated options both support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). We'll include a short runbook for key rotation and KMS integration in the follow-up pack.

Next actions (owners / ETA):
- Ben: capacity + cost estimate (draft) --- ETA Tue 12/1 COB.
- David: deployment diagram + KMS runbook (draft) --- ETA Tue 12/1 COB.
- Alex / Acme: populate acme_slo_requirements.xlsx with hourly qps and attach any anonymized sample logs --- ETA Mon 11/30 EOD.
- Marissa: schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive for Wed 12/2 10:00-11:00 PST (provisional) and share Zoom + Drive folder.
